text:
Here are the best Git commands to see file changes in the last commit:

## 1. Quick Preview

```bash
# Show which files changed + stats
git show --stat HEAD

# Show actual content diff
git show HEAD
```

## 2. File List Only

```bash
# Just file names
git log --name-only -1

# With commit message
git log --name-status -1
```

## 3. Diff Between Last Two Commits

```bash
# Show differences between HEAD and previous commit
git diff HEAD~1 HEAD
```

## 4. Tree View (Files in commit)

```bash
# See all files in last commit
git ls-tree HEAD

# See files added/modified/removed
git diff --name-status HEAD~1..HEAD
```

## 5. Summary Table

| Command | What It Shows | Best For |
|---------|--------------|----------|
| `git show HEAD` | Full commit + content | **Quick inspection** |
| `git log --name-status -1` | File names only | **File list** |
| `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` | Line-by-line changes | **Review changes** |
| `git show --stat HEAD` | Stats + file names | **Summary view** |

## Pro Tip: Follow the changes

```bash
# Navigate to the changed files in the last commit
git show HEAD --name-only --format='' | xargs git show HEAD:
```

## Quick Workflow

```bash
# 1. See what changed
git log --oneline -1

# 2. See file names
git show --name-only HEAD

# 3. Review content
git show HEAD
```

**TL;DR:** Use `git show HEAD` for everything, or `git log --name-only -1` for just file names! 🎯
